entries.notes: We are presently two wimmin living on the land and two wimmin living in different cities who share financial/emotional responsibilities for caretaking 40 acres. We are an intentional family of four who enjoy the support of several other extended family members who visit regularly to help with the farmwork and enjoy its special energy. Our interests include spiritual tolerance and development, organic farming, prosperity thinking and being, networking, and providing a working example of an alternative to patriarchal patterns. We give training in survival back to the earth skills: organic gardening, woodswomanship, natural healing, carpentry, plumbing, etc.

entries.notes: (7 mi from Monticello). Spiral is an all wimmin's space, open to membership. Supportive Membership is for wimmin to use the land for camping/workshops or just to be supportive. Community Membership entitles one to live here, be part of the community and own one's own improvements. In brief, our purposes say: To hold land in perpetuity, for wimmin to form community, to grow food organically, to provide education of alternative skills, etc.

entries.notes: (NW Michigan 1 hr from Traverse City - Jordan River Valley). In May '85 land, with two smallish houses, a barn, apple trees, critters and nature spirits, was purchased. We see our primary focus as a spiritual. one, experiencing. and developing our psychic, spiritual and nature-all inter-connectedness with a commitment to aid the healing of the Earth Mother. Our spirituality is eclectic in its background and manifestations, but has a decidedly Lesbian Feminist emphasis. The community space is considered basically vegetarian and incomes are shared. Future goals include sponsoring wimmin's gatherings and events, creating ongoing Lesbian spiritual circles, establishing a liaison with area Native wimmin and offering a healing, contemplative space to wimmin needing sanctuary.

entries.notes: (Atwood, on Lake Michigan in NW lower peninsula). We live in a clean and sober, nicotine-free 80-year-old stone cabin with 2 cats. We have a car, truck and motorcycle, a 30' x 50' garden, a foundation for another building, and septic and electrical hookups available for a trailer. Many adjoining acreages for sale. Visions are for a woodworking collective, berry and fruit farm, writer's hermitage, and horses once the land is paid off (Dec '86).

entries.notes: WWLC owns DOE (Daughters of Earth) Farm. The land is hilly, secluded, and very beautiful; half wooded campground (some chemical free space), half hayfield, orchard, garden, berries, etc., in west central Wisconsin. Four year-round residents, more in summer. Ten-year anniversary in '87. Sliding scale fees.

entries.notes: (Between Bastrop and Lockhart, south of Austin). The Hermitage is located on 9 acres of wooded land with Post Oak, Cedar, and Mesquite. On this land we are creating a space for women to discover themselves as whole women. We as women with our experiences on this planet have a strong need to heal.
